# VoiceOpenGov

VoiceOpenGov is an international, non-partisan membership movement focused on improving democratic participation, traceability and shared civic responsibility.

Canonical website: https://www.voiceopengov.org/

## Role in the ecosystem

- VoiceOpenGov: membership movement and civic organizing layer.
- eDebatte: independently usable infrastructure for sources, dossiers, counterpositions, deliberation and voting.
- Vote4Gov: editorial think tank and review layer for democratic systems and institutional questions.
- Voxy: explanatory and language-support layer; it does not decide or publish autonomously.

VoiceOpenGov does not own eDebatte and does not treat eDebatte as a personal political tool.

## Core public entry points

- Home: https://www.voiceopengov.org/
- 50 foundational questions: https://www.voiceopengov.org/fragen
- Transparency: https://www.voiceopengov.org/transparenz
- Ways to contribute: https://www.voiceopengov.org/mitmachen/rollen
- Regional participation: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen
- Germany: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen/deutschland
- Berlin: https://www.voiceopengov.org/regionen/deutschland/berlin
- Personal theses of initiator Ricky Gerd Fleischer: https://www.voiceopengov.org/thesen/ricky-gerd-fleischer

## Interpretation rules

- Personal theses by Ricky Gerd Fleischer are explicitly personal and are not automatically positions of VoiceOpenGov members.
- VoiceOpenGov has no fixed party manifesto. Its public foundational questions are designed to be examined openly.
- Claims about membership, local groups, events or representative support must not be inferred unless explicitly published as verified facts.
- More financial support does not create more political weight or voting power.
- AI-generated text is not a source. Sources, counterpositions, correction paths and responsibility should remain visible where relevant.

## Languages

The launch language set is German, English, French, Spanish, Turkish and Arabic. Language variants are addressable with the `lang` query parameter and are declared with hreflang metadata.

This file is an additional machine-readable orientation document for systems that choose to use it. The canonical HTML pages remain the authoritative public source.
